references.text: The children of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron earlier in the wilderness, showing a repeated pattern of rebellion against their leaders.

This is the direct parallel in some Bible translations (verse 17:6 in the Hebrew text corresponds to 16:41 in other numbering systems), where the congregation grumbled against Moses and Aaron the day after Korah's rebellion.
The context for the accusation 'you have killed the Lord's people' refers to the judgment over Korah, Dathan, and Abiram and the 250 men who were consumed by fire.
The children of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sin, an early example of the people's complaints against their leaders.
The people contended with Moses at Rephidim, showing the persistent pattern of complaints against Moses' leadership.
The whole congregation wanted to stone Moses and Aaron, demonstrating the seriousness of the hostility toward their leaders.
The congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron at Kadesh because of a lack of water, another example of the people's repeated rebellion.
